title: Instagram Feed: Complete Architecture
description: Design an Instagram-like photo and video sharing platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a photo and video sharing platform like Instagram. Users upload media with captions, apply filters, like and comment on posts, follow other users, and browse a personalized feed. The system must support Stories that expire after 24 hours, an Explore page for discovery, and real-time notifications for engagement.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Upload photos and videos with captions, location tags, and multiple media per post
Apply real-time filters and basic edits before publishing
Like, unlike, comment, save/bookmark, and share posts
Follow and unfollow users with private account approval flows
Generate personalized home feed using follow graph and engagement signals
Stories: photo/video clips visible for 24 hours with view tracking
Explore page: algorithmically ranked content from non-followed accounts
Direct messaging with media sharing and ephemeral story replies
Push notifications for likes, comments, follows, and mentions
Content moderation queue for auto-flagged and human-reviewed media

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-200ms feed generation at P99 with edge caching for hot content
99.9% availability for read traffic, 99.5% for uploads
Support 1 billion+ media objects with infinite horizontal scale
Eventual consistency for likes and follower counts (tolerate stale counts)
Strong consistency for user authentication and posting ownership
Global CDN distribution for media assets with origin shield
Real-time notification delivery within 5 seconds of engagement
Content moderation latency under 2 seconds for auto-scanned media

data.text: Build a monolithic ASP.NET Core API with SQL Server. Use Entity Framework Core for posts, users, comments, and follows. Store media in Azure Blob Storage with CDN fronting. Implement basic feed generation via SQL joins on the follow graph. This validates the content model, upload flow, and simple ranking.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API with clean architecture
  - Entity Framework Core with SQL Server
  - Azure SQL Database for users, posts, comments, follows
  - Azure Blob Storage + CDN for media delivery
  - Azure Cognitive Services (Vision) for content moderation
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service for hosting
  - Azure Redis Cache for feed pre-computation
  - Azure Service Bus for async notifications
  - Single database with tables: Users, Posts, Media, Comments, Likes, Follows, Stories

data.text: Split into microservices by domain: Feed Service pre-computes timelines using fan-out-on-write, Post Service manages content creation, Media Service handles uploads and transformations, Recommendation Service powers Explore, and Notification Service handles engagement alerts.

items: Feed Service: Implements fan-out-on-write by pushing new posts to follower timelines at publish time, caches pre-computed feeds in Redis sorted sets, and falls back to on-read merge for users with millions of followers.
Post Service: Handles post creation, edits, deletions, and caption processing, manages post visibility rules (private accounts, blocked users), and emits PostCreated events for feed fan-out.

Media Service: Accepts multipart uploads, generates variants (thumbnail, preview, full-res), applies CDN cache headers, and triggers content moderation scans via Azure Cognitive Services or AWS Rekognition.
User Service: Manages profiles, follow/unfollow actions, follower/following counts, private account approvals, and blocked user relationships.
Notification Service: Processes engagement events (like, comment, follow, mention), aggregates per-user notification feeds, and dispatches push/in-app alerts via SignalR and FCM/APNS.
Recommendation Service: Powers the Explore page using collaborative filtering and content-based ranking, ingests engagement signals, and serves ranked post candidates via gRPC for low latency.

        useFilterPreview.ts      # CSS/canvas filter pipeline
        useIntersectionObserver.ts # Lazy media loading
      store/

        uploadSlice.ts           # Upload queue, retries
  shared/
    ui/
    lib/
    hooks/

Key Patterns:
  - Virtualized list for feed performance (react-window)
  - Intersection Observer for lazy media and ad impressions
  - Offline draft saving for posts in progress
  - Web Workers for client-side image/video compression
  - Optimistic like with rollback on API failure

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Social feeds are read-heavy - pre-compute timelines with fan-out-on-write for users with < 1M followers
Media is the bulk of storage - use CDN with origin shield and auto-generated variants
Eventual consistency is acceptable for likes and counts; strong consistency for ownership and auth
Recommendation systems require separate feature stores and ML pipelines
Content moderation must be async to avoid blocking user uploads
data.takeaway: Instagram is a media-heavy social graph system. Optimize the read path with edge caching and pre-computed feeds, separate media processing from business logic, and accept eventual consistency for engagement metrics to maximize availability.
